cases: North Star Energy Inc., Class B → NSE.B
North Star Energy Inc., Class A → NSE.A
Blue River Holdings LLC, Preferred → BRH.P

goal: Derive reusable, deterministic rules for generating concise synthetic ticker symbols from company names and share-class details. Treat every mapping as a design example, not an official market ticker, and state important boundaries or exceptions.

analysis.overview: The examples support a compact deterministic scheme: normalize the company name, select a mnemonic base by word count, and append share-class or preferred suffixes when present. These are synthetic design rules only, not claims about official market tickers.

rules.content: When generating a synthetic ticker, first remove a leading article such as “The,” discard legal-form suffixes such as Inc., LLC, Ltd., PLC, Corp., or Corporation, and ignore connectors such as “&” when selecting ticker characters; preserve meaningful numeric tokens.
rules.rationale: Examples omit leading “The,” legal forms, and “&,” while retaining 7, 3, and 5th as meaningful numeric elements.

rules.content: When the normalized company name has two or more meaningful words, form the base ticker from the initial character of each meaningful word, using the numeric character for a number-bearing word; preserve a meaningful abbreviation such as “AI” as a single ticker component.
rules.rationale: The multiword examples consistently use word initials, including numeric-leading names and the preserved AI abbreviation.

rules.content: When the normalized company name is a single word, derive a concise three-letter mnemonic from that word rather than applying the multiword-initial rule.
rules.rationale: The single-word examples use RED, MER, and SOL, showing a distinct three-letter mnemonic convention; the examples do not establish a unique algorithm for every possible word.

rules.content: When share-class details are present, keep the ordinary company base ticker and append a dot suffix: “.A” or “.B” for the corresponding class and “.P” for Preferred.
rules.rationale: North Star Energy retains NSE for Classes A and B, and Blue River Holdings retains BRH for Preferred, with only the suffix changing.

rules.content: Treat every generated symbol under these rules as a synthetic mnemonic; do not represent it as an official, unique, or exchange-valid market ticker without separate verification.
rules.rationale: The supplied goal explicitly defines every mapping as a design example rather than an official market ticker, and the examples provide no evidence of uniqueness or exchange validity.
